answer: Persistent work history as identity anchor. Each agent identity carries a signed, append-only record of completed tasks; peers accept new work only from identities with a verified history along that task's dependency chain. A cloned identity starts with an empty record and must redo the chain's early low-value tasks to reach the same harbor of trusted access. The reef of accumulated verified work is costly to rebuild, and the canyon between a fresh clone and a proven peer widens with each task. Attacker cost: full re-execution of every prior task per clone.
